_comment: Bridge-1 campaign build manifest. The campaign ports C++ into an EXISTING Rust crate
(crates/compiler/deeptools); there is no C build to configure, no shim to compile and no FFI
boundary, so `configure` is a no-op and the C-side gates in the translator playbook do not apply.
⛔ TRANSLATOR GATE — run EXACTLY these two, from the repo root, ONCE PER BATCH:
cargo check -p deeptools
cargo test  -p deeptools
Both are seconds-to-a-minute: `deeptools` has one path dependency (sys-arch-spec) and no
registry deps. DO NOT run the workspace-wide or acceptance build in an agent worktree — its
target/ is ~6 GB and this host has under 75 GB free with a second campaign running; the
orchestrator owns that gate and runs it once per landed sub-campaign.
⛔ THE CRATE'S OWN ACCEPTANCE IS BOTH MODELS, BOTH OR NEITHER
(crates/compiler/deeptools/CLAUDE.md):
cargo build -Fsuperdsc,model/granite-3.1-2b-instruct,quant/fp8-dynamic-per-channel
cargo build -Fsuperdsc,model/granite-3.1-8b-instruct,quant/fp8-dynamic-per-channel
8b is hd=128/4096/12800 vs 2b's 64/2048/8192 — a different door arm and tile geometry, so 2b
passing HIDES defects 8b finds. Neither links on this Mac: `superdsc` on the CLI turns on
scratchy-serving-worker/sendnn -> flex-rs, whose build.rs cc-compiles a senlib shim against
/opt/ibm/spyre/senlib/include — Spyre-host-only headers. The `pipeline` command below is the
largest runnable prefix that still expands #[forward] and therefore still runs this bridge
over every staged program.
_comment_cpp: There is a C++ translation unit in the campaign (cpp/bridge1.cpp) but nothing builds it. It is
an INDEX: which function, in what order, and where its original lives.
✅ ITS BODIES ARE VERIFIED VERBATIM AND UNTRUNCATED — 110 of 110, by tools/verify_extract.py,
which re-derives every function's end from the authority with its OWN brace matcher and compares
LENGTHS and CONTENT. It never re-slices with the extractor's own (file, line, length): that
tautology is what let bridge 2 report 'verbatim, 12 sampled, none differed' over a corpus where
366 of 384 bodies were truncated. Two negative controls confirm the check bites.
⚠ cpp/prelude.inc does NOT make the unit compile, and no gate requires it to. These bodies do
heavy member access on opaque reference types (mlir::Value, OpBuilder, dsc2::*), which no
behaviour-free stand-in can satisfy without the real headers — bridge 2 stopped at ~500
name-resolution errors for the same reason. prelude.inc catalogues the 116 qualified scopes and
217 external calls the bodies reach, so the unit is self-describing.
